'''Gion Shrine''' (祇園神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the {{ill|Kojima Area|de|GermanName|ja|児島地域 (倉敷市)|lt=Kojima area|lt_ja=児島地域|lt_de=GermanName|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11388647}} of {{ill|Kurashiki|en|Kurashiki|qid=Q467487|lt=Kurashiki City}}, {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|Okayama Prefecture|qid=Q132936|lt=Okayama Prefecture}}. It is also called '''Shimotsui Gion Jinja''' (下津井祇園神社).

== Deities ==
They enshrine {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|de|GermanName|ja|素戔嗚尊|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|lt_ja=素戔嗚尊|lt_de=GermanName|qid=Q272993}} as the main deity, along with {{ill|Kushinadahime|de|GermanName|ja|奇稲田姫命|lt=Kushinada-hime|lt_ja=奇稲田姫命|lt_de=GermanName|qid=Q505469|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q505469}}, {{ill|Orochi no Aramasa|de|GermanName|ja|蛇の麁正|lt=Ōrochi no Aramasa}}, Nagahama-no-Kami, Hassha Daimyōjin, and {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|de|GermanName|ja|事代主神|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Kami|lt_ja=事代主神|lt_de=GermanName|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q8009611}}. They are believed to bring blessings for maritime safety and protection against epidemics.

== History ==
[[File:The Inland Sea is faced from the Gion Shinto shrine.JPG|thumb|right|250px|A view of the Seto Inland Sea from the shrine precinct]]
'''Gion Shrine''' is the ujigami (tutelary deity) of the {{ill|Shimotsui|de|GermanName|ja|下津井地区|lt=Shimotsui district|lt_ja=下津井地区|lt_de=GermanName|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11361095}}, affectionately referred to as “Gion-san.” It is enshrined on top of Mount Jōyama (浄山), which juts out over the sea at an elevation of 22 meters. When it was merged with the Gion-gū, two connected main sanctuaries were formed. In addition, the present approach to the shrine was donated by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|de|GermanName|ja|池田氏#美濃池田家|lt=Ikeda clan|lt_ja=池田氏|lt_de=GermanName|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2975277}} in the 3rd year of {{ill|Bunkyū|en|Bunkyū|qid=Q730266|lt=Bunkyū}} ({{ill|1863|en|1863|qid=Q7701|lt=1863}}). In former times, there was a thriving ryotei (traditional restaurant) called “Kinparō” at the foot of the hill, but it was burned down in an arson fire in June of Heisei 8 (1996).

The year of Gion Jinja’s founding is unknown. Its precincts originally corresponded to the ruins of the old Nagahama Castle, which was built around the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}. In the {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period}}, it was founded as the guardian shrine of that castle, known then as “Nagahama-gū” or “Nagahama Daimyōjin.” Around the latter half of the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, it was merged with the Gion-gū and became “Gion Jinja.” In modern times, it was renamed “Susanoo Jinja” in December of {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji}} 3 ({{ill|1871|en|1871|qid=Q7746|lt=1871}}), but then returned to the name “Gion Jinja” in September of Meiji 21 ({{ill|1888|en|1888|qid=Q7829|lt=1888}}). Later, in Meiji 43 ({{ill|1910|en|1910|qid=Q2075|lt=1910}}), “Hachihashira Jinja” was also merged here.

Since ancient times, this location was the scene of numerous battles. During the {{ill|Genpei War|en|Genpei War|qid=Q737542|lt=Genpei War}}, it is said {{ill|Taira clan|de|GermanName|ja|平家|lt=Taira clan}} forces used it as a stronghold in preparation for the {{ill|Battle of Ichi-no-Tani|en|Battle of Ichi-no-Tani|qid=Q2116658|lt=Battle of Ichi-no-Tani}} on the {{ill|Honshu|en|Honshu|qid=Q13989|lt=Honshū}} side. After a contingent of the Taira had crossed over from {{ill|Shikoku|en|Shikoku|qid=Q13991|lt=Shikoku}}, a group of Shikoku warriors switched allegiance to the {{ill|Minamoto clan|en|Minamoto clan|qid=Q599881|lt=Minamoto clan}} and sailed with around a dozen warships to attack the waters off Shimotsui. Because the Taira generals such as {{ill|Taira no Norimori|en|Taira no Norimori|qid=Q11060997|lt=Taira no Norimori}}, {{ill|Taira no Tomomori|de|GermanName|ja|平通盛|lt=Taira no Tomomori|lt_ja=平通盛|lt_de=GermanName|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11483584}}, and {{ill|Taira no Noritsune|en|Taira no Noritsune|qid=Q1189315|lt=Taira no Kiyotsune}} were entrenched here, the attackers were easily driven back to Shikoku. Later, during the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|en|Nanboku-chō period|qid=Q264012|lt=Nanboku-chō period}}, it is recorded that {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|ar|أشيكاغا تاكا-أوجي|ca|Ashikaga Takauji|cs|Takaudži Ašikaga|de|Ashikaga Takauji|es|Ashikaga Takauji|eu|Ashikaga Takauji|fa|آشیکاگا تاکائوجی|fi|Ashikaga Takauji|fr|Ashikaga Takauji|hak|Ashikaga Takauji|he|אשיקאגה טאקאוג'י|hu|Asikaga Takaudzsi|id|Ashikaga Takauji|it|Ashikaga Takauji|ja|足利尊氏|ko|아시카가 다카우지|mr|अशिकागा तकाउजी|nl|Ashikaga Takauji|pl|Takauji Ashikaga|pt|Ashikaga Takauji|ru|Асикага Такаудзи|simple|Ashikaga Takauji|sr|Ашикага Такауџи|sv|Ashikaga Takauji|th|อาชิกางะ ทากาอูจิ|tr|Ashikaga Takauji|uk|Асікаґа Такаудзі|vi|Ashikaga Takauji|zh|足利尊氏|zh_min_nan|Asikaga Takauzi|zh_yue|足利尊氏|qid=Q297107|lt=Ashikaga Takauji}}, leading more than a thousand warships from {{ill|Kyushu|en|Kyushu|qid=Q13987|lt=Kyūshū}}, stayed in this area for several days en route to the east.

== Festivals ==
* 3rd Saturday and Sunday in July: Gion Festival
* 4th Saturday and Sunday in October: Nagahama Festival

== Sacred Grove ==
Because the shrine precinct is situated on a small promontory above the {{ill|Seto Inland Sea|en|Seto Inland Sea|qid=Q231312|lt=Seto Inland Sea}}, the surrounding grove (the chinju no mori) features many coastal plant species. In particular, the grove is notable for large stands of {{ill|Quercus phillyreoides|en|Quercus phillyreoides|qid=Q10877943|lt=Ubamegashi}}, known for producing binchōtan charcoal. There is also the broadleaf evergreen {{ill|Cleyera japonica var. grandis|de|GermanName|ja|クスドイゲ|qid=Q12600055|lt=Kusudo-ige}}, which is rare in this region and of academic value. Formerly, a unique weeping cherry tree (Gion-shidare) stood in front of the main shrine, but it has since died. Altogether, around 30 species (including both wild and planted) compose this shrine forest, which was designated an Okayama Prefectural Folk Cultural Property in Showa 56 (1981).<ref>[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/seikatsu/sizen/sizenkouen.etc/area/417shimotsui.html 岡山県環境文化部自然環境課、「下津井祇園神社の社叢」（おかやまの自然公園）].</ref>

== Stored Materials ==
“Gion Documents” (Gion Monjo), records from the late Edo period relating to this shrine, are designated Important Cultural Properties of Kurashiki City. They include information on business practices of the time and donations made to the shrine, reflecting the economic prosperity of Shimotsui.<ref>[http://www.city.kurashiki.okayama.jp/dd.aspx?menuid=5481 倉敷市役所、「下津井祇園文書」].</ref> Additionally, the model of the {{ill|gozabune|ja|御座船|no|Gozabune|qid=Q11489006|lt=御za-bune}} “Hakō-maru,” the official boat of the {{ill|Okayama Domain|fa|قلمرو اوکایاما|fr|Domaine d'Okayama|ja|岡山藩|ko|오카야마번|ru|Окаяма (княжество)|zh|岡山藩|qid=Q903497|lt=Bizen Domain}}, was donated in {{ill|Bunka|en|Bunka|qid=Q1373146|lt=1811 (Bunka 8)}} by {{ill|Ikeda Narimasa|ja|池田斉政|ko|이케다 나리마사|qid=Q11551949|lt=Ikeda Narimasa}} to the Nagahama-gū and Gion-gū shrines in Shimotsui. Built at a 1/10 scale, the entire hull is finished in lacquer with patches of {{ill|Gold leaf|ar|صفيحة ذهبية|be|Сусальнае золата|bn|সোনালি পাতা|ca|Pa d'or|cv|Лапташка ылттăн|da|Bladguld|de|Blattgold|eo|Orfolio|es|Pan de oro|et|Lehtkuld|eu|Urre-xafla|fa|روکش طلا|fi|Lehtikulta|fr|Feuille d'or|he|עלי זהב (חומר)|hr|Zlatni listići|id|Kertas emas|is|Blaðgull|it|Foglia oro|ja|金箔|ka|ოქროფურცელი|ko|금박|mn|Ялтсан алт|ms|Daun emas|nl|Bladgoud|nn|Bladgull|no|Bladgull|pl|Złoto płatkowe|pt|Folha de ouro|ro|Foiță de aur|ru|Сусальное золото|simple|Gold leaf|sq|Fleta e arit|th|ทองคำเปลว|uk|Сухозлітне золото|ur|سونے کا ورق|vi|Vàng quỳ|zh|金箔|qid=Q929186|lt=gold leaf}} and decorative metal fittings. In the past, this model was carried on a {{ill|danjiri|ja|だんじり|qid=Q11271630|lt=danjiri}} float during festivals, but it is now preserved in the shrine’s storage facility.<ref>[http://www.city.kurashiki.okayama.jp/dd.aspx?menuid=5467 倉敷市役所、「御座船模型」].</ref>
